paper_b.title: Score-Based Generative Modeling through Stochastic Differential Equations

metadata.description: Parallel rediscovery: DDPM (Ho-Jain-Abbeel) and Score SDE (Song et al.) independently arrive at essentially the same generative diffusion procedure. DDPM works in discrete time with a Gaussian Markov chain, an epsilon-prediction parameterization, and a re-weighted variational bound; Score SDE writes the same construction in continuous time as a forward Ito SDE plus Anderson's reverse-time SDE driven by the score. Score SDE explicitly identifies DDPM's forward chain as a discretization of its VP SDE and DDPM's ancestral sampler as a discretization of the corresponding reverse-time SDE, and rewrites L_simple as denoising score matching. The papers thus describe the same object in dual languages (discrete-time epsilon-prediction vs continuous-time score).

matches.explanation: DDPM's forward Markov chain q(x_t|x_{t-1}) = N(sqrt(1-beta_t) x_{t-1}, beta_t I) is the same object that Score SDE both restates as the DDPM perturbation kernel (DP231.4) and identifies as the Euler-Maruyama discretization of the VP SDE (DP231.8). Score SDE's Appendix B derivation (PP231.3) explicitly takes the limit of DDPM's chain to obtain the VP SDE, so the discrete and continuous formulations are the same forward process up to time-stepping.

DDPM's learned reverse Markov chain p_theta(x_{t-1}|x_t) with Gaussian transitions is the discrete-time form of the continuous reverse-time SDE (DP231.6) given by Anderson's theorem (TP231.1). Score SDE's PrP231.2 / PP231.5 explicitly proves that DDPM ancestral sampling is a discretization of the same reverse-time VP SDE, so the underlying generative reverse process is identical.

DDPM's notation alpha_t = 1 - beta_t and bar-alpha_t = prod alpha_s appears verbatim in Score SDE's DDPM forward-chain restatement (DP231.4 uses alpha_i := prod_{j<=i}(1 - beta_j)); the symbol 'alpha' is reused with the same definition.

DDPM's closed-form forward marginal q(x_t|x_0) = N(sqrt(bar-alpha_t) x_0, (1 - bar-alpha_t) I) is exactly the DDPM/VP perturbation kernel restated in Score SDE (DP231.4), and is the special case of EP231.5 (closed-form Gaussian perturbation kernels for VE/VP/sub-VP) for the VP SDE.

The closed-form discrete-time conditioned posterior q(x_{t-1}|x_t,x_0) is a DDPM-specific object used to write its Rao-Blackwellized variational bound. Score SDE bypasses this construction entirely — it works at the SDE level with the score function and Anderson's reversal — so there is no direct counterpart.

DDPM's epsilon-prediction parameterization mu_theta(x_t,t) = (1/sqrt(alpha_t))(x_t - (beta_t/sqrt(1-bar-alpha_t)) eps_theta) plays the same role as Score SDE's score network s_theta(x,t) ~ grad log p_t(x) (DP231.1): both are the learned function that drives the reverse update. They differ by an affine reparameterization eps_theta = -sqrt(1-bar-alpha_t) s_theta. Same conceptual role (learned drift correction), different but interconvertible parameterization.

The discretized Gaussian decoder p_theta(x_0|x_1) for image-pixel output is a DDPM-specific contribution tied to lossless-codelength evaluation on integer pixel data. Score SDE works with continuous data (with uniform dequantization noted in RP231.3) and has no analogous discrete decoder.

DDPM's variational bound on NLL and its KL decomposition into L_T + sum L_{t-1} + L_0 are the discrete-time ELBO machinery inherited from Sohl-Dickstein. Score SDE does not write an ELBO — it trains via a continuous denoising score-matching objective (EP231.3) and computes likelihoods via the probability flow ODE (AP231.10). No direct counterpart to the per-step KL decomposition.

DDPM's epsilon-MSE form of L_{t-1} (EP230.5) and the simplified objective L_simple (EP230.6) are the same loss family as Score SDE's DDPM re-weighted ELBO objective (EP231.2 — explicitly rewritten as denoising score matching with weight (1-alpha_i)) and as the discrete-N specialization of the continuous score-matching objective (EP231.3). Score SDE's RP231.1 makes the equivalence explicit. Same loss, written in noise-prediction (DDPM) vs score-prediction (Score SDE) language.

DDPM's alternate variational bound L = KL(q(x_T)||p(x_T)) + sum KL(q(x_{t-1}|x_t)||p_theta(x_{t-1}|x_t)) + H(x_0) and its autoregressive interpretation (PrP230.3) are unique DDPM-side observations used to discuss progressive coding and a generalized bit ordering. Score SDE has no analogue of this alternate bound.

DDPM's progressive estimate hat-x_0 = (x_t - sqrt(1-bar-alpha_t) eps_theta(x_t))/sqrt(bar-alpha_t) (Tweedie-type one-step denoising) is implicit in Score SDE's RP231.2 (Tweedie denoising step at t=0) but is not lifted to a named object in the Score SDE graph; conservatively recorded as none on the L1 nodes.

DDPM's Proposition PrP230.1 — that the epsilon-prediction VB term equals (up to a t-dependent weight) a denoising score matching loss — is exactly the equivalence Score SDE's RP231.1 records when stating that SMLD's sigma_i^2 weight and DDPM's (1-alpha_i) weight both correspond to inverse expected score-norm, exposing DDPM/SMLD as the same weighted denoising score-matching family. Same equivalence, stated as a proposition in DDPM and as a remark in Score SDE.

The Rao-Blackwellized KL decomposition of L into per-step Gaussian KLs is a DDPM-side proposition tied to its discrete variational bound. Score SDE does not derive an analogous per-step decomposition (it uses the SDE / Fokker-Planck framework instead).
DDPM's reinterpretation of diffusion as a generalized autoregressive model (with a special masking schedule and T = D) is a paper-specific conceptual remark with no Score SDE counterpart.

DDPM's training algorithm (sample x_0, t, eps; SGD on ||eps - eps_theta||^2) is the discrete-N realization of Score SDE's continuous-time score-matching training objective (EP231.3), with weight schedule (1-alpha_i) (EP231.2). Score SDE does not present a separate named training algorithm node — the training objective IS the algorithm — so the match is L1-algorithm to L1-equation, hence analogous.

DDPM's sampling algorithm AP230.2 is exactly Score SDE's cited DDPM ancestral sampler (AP231.13) and is rederived as the predictor in Score SDE's PC sampler for the VP SDE (AP231.3 — same iterate up to the epsilon/score reparameterization). PrP231.2 and PP231.5 explicitly prove this is a discretization of the reverse-time VP SDE.

DDPM's progressive lossy sender/receiver protocols using minimal random coding are a unique DDPM-side contribution interpreting the variational bound as a codelength. Score SDE has no compression/coding angle (its likelihood story uses the probability flow ODE instead, which is a different idea — see AP231.10).

Both papers state the same problem: train a generative model on natural-image data using a learned reverse of a fixed Gaussian noising process and produce high-quality samples (CIFAR10, CelebA-HQ, LSUN are common benchmarks). Score SDE phrases it as score-based modeling via SDEs (ProbP231.1); DDPM phrases it as high-fidelity image generation with diffusion models (ProbP230.1). Same problem, equivalent formulations.

Appendix B derivation of DDPM's KL decomposition of L is unique to the discrete-time variational-bound treatment (see EP230.2 / PrP230.2 above). Score SDE's PP231.1 (Fokker-Planck / probability flow) is a different derivation for a different theorem.

DDPM's derivation of the epsilon-MSE form of L_{t-1} is the DDPM-side proof that L_simple is a weighted denoising score matching loss. Score SDE assumes/cites this equivalence (RP231.1) without rederiving it as a labeled proof. Conservatively marked none on the L1-proof level.
Derivation of the alternate VB EP230.7 is DDPM-specific (mirrors EP230.7 / PrP230.3); no Score SDE counterpart.

DDPM's discussion of differences from NCSN (architecture, scaling, schedule) refers to the same NCSN object that Score SDE formalizes as its noise-conditional score network (DP231.3) and annealed Langevin sampler (AP231.12). Both papers position their construction relative to NCSN; the alignment is at the 'related-work' level.

Both papers report unconditional CIFAR-10 generation as their headline benchmark (DDPM: IS 9.46, FID 3.17; Score SDE: IS 9.89, FID 2.20 — Score SDE explicitly improves over DDPM on the same metric/dataset).

Both papers showcase CelebA-HQ samples and latent-space interpolations. DDPM uses 256x256 with linear interpolation in x_t; Score SDE uses spherical interpolation on probability-flow latent codes. Same demonstration, different latent construction.

DDPM's LSUN Bedroom/Church/Cat sample-quality benchmarks are mentioned only in passing in Score SDE (which uses LSUN for inpainting/colorization, ExP231.5, not for FID benchmarking). No precise example-level counterpart.
DDPM's rate-distortion curve on CIFAR10 is a unique DDPM-side experiment supporting its codelength interpretation; Score SDE has no rate-distortion analysis.

DDPM's progressive generation demo (showing hat-x_0 at intermediate steps) is conceptually echoed in Score SDE's discussion of the probability-flow latent code (ExP231.6, ExP231.7) but not directly mirrored as an example.

Both papers cite Sohl-Dickstein et al. 2015 as the diffusion-probabilistic-models foundation. In Score SDE this prior result is folded into the DDPM-chain definition DP231.4 (which co-cites Sohl-Dickstein 2015 and Ho et al. 2020). External-vs-external cross-citation, no signal for relation_type.

DDPM's cited NCSN result (denoising score matching with annealed Langevin dynamics) is exactly Score SDE's NCSN definition (DP231.3), SMLD denoising score-matching objective (EP231.1), and annealed Langevin algorithm (AP231.12), all attributed to Song & Ermon 2019. External citation match.

Score SDE's SMLD perturbation kernel p_sigma(tilde-x|x) = N(x, sigma^2 I) over multiple noise scales is the variance-exploding noise model from Song & Ermon 2019. DDPM uses a different (variance-preserving) Markov-chain perturbation and never builds the SMLD kernel; this is a Score-SDE-side construction with no DDPM counterpart.

The continuous-time forward Ito SDE dx = f(x,t) dt + g(t) dw is the central Score-SDE-side abstraction. DDPM stays entirely in discrete time and never writes the SDE; the closest object on the DDPM side is the discrete forward chain DP230.2, which is matched separately as the (VP-)discretization.
The variance-exploding (VE) SDE is Score SDE's continuous-time limit of the SMLD chain; DDPM has no VE construction (it uses variance-preserving noise).
The sub-VP SDE is a Score-SDE-side novel construction with tighter variance bound than VP; not present in DDPM.

The probability flow ODE (DP231.10), its marginal-equivalence theorem (TP231.2), and the Fokker-Planck-based proof (PP231.1) are unique Score-SDE contributions enabling deterministic sampling and exact-likelihood evaluation. DDPM has no deterministic sampler and no analogous ODE.
The general matrix-diffusion SDE with state-dependent G(x,t) is Score SDE's most general continuous-time form (Appendix A); DDPM has no such generalization.

Conditional / inverse-problem sampling — conditional reverse-time SDE (DP231.12, TP231.4), the conditional sampling problem (ProbP231.2), imputation (AP231.7), colorization (AP231.8), and classifier-guided class-conditional sampling (AP231.9) — is a major Score-SDE-side contribution that DDPM does not address.
Sliced-score-matching variant of the training objective is a Score-SDE-side fallback for non-affine drifts; DDPM has no analogue (it uses denoising score matching only).
The variance bound sub-VP <= VP and its proof are unique Score-SDE contributions tied to the sub-VP SDE construction (DP231.9); no DDPM counterpart.

Score SDE's Proposition that the DDPM ancestral sampler matches reverse-diffusion sampling of the VP SDE in the limit (and its Appendix-F proof) is a Score-SDE-side bridging result. The corresponding DDPM-side claim (that AP230.2 equals the reverse-time SDE discretization) is not stated in DDPM's graph; logged here as Score-SDE-only.

Score SDE's Appendix-B derivations of the VE and VP SDEs as continuum limits of the SMLD/DDPM chains are Score-SDE-side proofs that connect the discrete and continuous formulations. DDPM never takes the continuous limit, so it has no analogous proof.

The Predictor-Corrector sampler (general AP231.1, VE-specialization AP231.2, reverse-diffusion predictor AP231.4) is Score SDE's flagship sampler combining a numerical SDE solver with a score-based MCMC corrector. DDPM uses a single-shot ancestral sampler with no MCMC corrector; the PC framework has no DDPM counterpart.

Probability-flow ODE sampler (AP231.5), exact-likelihood computation via probability flow + Hutchinson trace estimator (AP231.10, EP231.6), and the exact-likelihood-evaluation problem (ProbP231.3) are all Score-SDE-side contributions enabled by the deterministic ODE. DDPM evaluates likelihood only via the variational bound (EP230.1).

Score SDE introduces an ancestral sampler for SMLD models (analogous derivation as DDPM's ancestral sampler but for the variance-exploding chain). DDPM does not consider SMLD/VE schedules, so there is no counterpart.

Annealed Langevin dynamics as a corrector with signal-to-noise step-size schedule is a Score-SDE-side algorithm (a generalization of NCSN's sampler used inside the PC framework). DDPM has no Langevin/MCMC corrector step in its sampler.

Score-SDE-side experimental contributions without direct DDPM counterparts: CIFAR-10 likelihood at 2.99 bits/dim via probability flow (ExP231.2), CelebA-HQ 1024x1024 (ExP231.3 — DDPM only goes to 256x256), class-conditional CIFAR-10 (ExP231.4), LSUN inpainting/colorization (ExP231.5), and unique-identifiability empirical verification (ExP231.6, an ODE-specific experiment).
